newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief concerned over violence in East Timor.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief concerned over violence in East Timor.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan expressed concern on Friday at reports of recent violence in the Indonesian-ruled former Portuguese colony of East Timor and called on all parties to exercise restraint.
At least 34 people have been reported killed as a result of attacks by separatists seeking to disrupt Indonesia's May 29 general election in East Timor.
The United Nations has never recognised Indonesia's authority over the territory, which it invaded in 1975 after the departure of Portugal and annexed the following year.

"The secretary-general has been following with concern the reports of the recent violent incidents in East Timor which have resulted in the loss of life and are causing considerable human suffering," a statement issued through a U.N. spokesman said.
"The secretary-general has called on all parties concerned to exercise restraint," it added.
Annan is scheduled to hold the next in a long-running series of meetings on East Timor with the foreign ministers of Indonesia and Portugal on June 19 and 20 in New York.
The meeting, to try to find an internationally acceptable solution to the issue, were initiated in 1983 by then Secretary-General Javier Perez de Cuellar of Peru.
